The main takeaway from our work is that

SPAG6 is required for normal ciliary function in the brain and lungs, and that SPAG16L has an overlapping role in the brain but not in the lung, and that the combined deficiency of these proteins causes more severe phenotypes than the individual deficiencies, especially in the lung.
SPAG6/16 double mutant mice die earlier and have more severe hydrocephalus and more severe lung disease than either single mutant.
SPAG6 is essential for normal function of the cilia in brain and lung.
